key_insight: The paper builds globally reliable and efficient computable error estimators for monotone nonlinear PDEs, and shows they can be used directly as loss functions for neural-network surrogate models.
engineering_relevance: This gives engineers a provably correct way to train and validate FEM surrogates or PINN-like models for parametric nonlinear systems without relying on near-solution assumptions.
method: Split the nonlinear operator into a linear residual plus a strongly monotone closure term.
Measure the linear part in a discrete dual norm and approximate the closure term with a computable surrogate.
Prove two-sided bounds with explicit constants for both conforming FOSLS and discontinuous Petrov-Galerkin settings.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical global reliability and efficiency results, with assumptions verified for a model class of nonlinear fluxes and constants tracked explicitly over the parameter range.
watch_item: The estimator depends on a surrogate for the closure dual norm, so practical performance hinges on satisfying the stated pairing and Lipschitz conditions in implementation.
paper_title: Global error estimators for parametric monotone nonlinearities and neural approximations
